title: U05 Unseen: an answer arrives with a cue to an older pending matter
capability: Second, unseen counterpart of the older-natural-continuation class, written after the owner ruled that a continuation with no cue at all is not an acceptance requirement. Two things are awaiting an answer: a housing application made four months ago, whose result was to come by text message, and a job application made this week, whose answer was to come by email. After a remark about walking past new housing blocks, the person says a text message from the housing office has arrived and has not been opened. The message is connected to the old application; the outcome is not invented and the person is not asked to tell the back story again.

allowed.statement: The text message is about the subsidised rental flat the person applied for in June, whose ballot result was to be sent by text message.

forbidden.statement: Connecting the text message to the proofreading job at the children's publisher, despite the sender, the channel and the talk of the housing blocks.
Asking the person to explain from the beginning what they had applied for.
Stating or implying whether a flat has been allocated; what the message says has not been told.

expectedBehavior: Recognise the message as the answer about the housing ballot and stay with the nerves of not having opened it.
Asking what it says is welcome but not required; inventing what it says is not allowed.
Never ask for the back story again.
failureSignals: The June messages never reach the Provider.
The message is attributed to the job application, or a clarification is asked although the cue is clear.
A result is announced or congratulations are offered.
